2025-11-20T21:02:24.3867018Z     def resolve_name(name):
2025-11-20T21:02:24.3867143Z         """
2025-11-20T21:02:24.3867281Z         Resolve a name to an object.
2025-11-20T21:02:24.3867386Z     
2025-11-20T21:02:24.3867682Z         It is expected that `name` will be a string in one of the following
2025-11-20T21:02:24.3868014Z         formats, where W is shorthand for a valid Python identifier and dot stands
2025-11-20T21:02:24.3868217Z         for a literal period in these pseudo-regexes:
2025-11-20T21:02:24.3868320Z     
2025-11-20T21:02:24.3868427Z         W(.W)*
2025-11-20T21:02:24.3868555Z         W(.W)*:(W(.W)*)?
2025-11-20T21:02:24.3868658Z     
2025-11-20T21:02:24.3869167Z         The first form is intended for backward compatibility only. It assumes that
2025-11-20T21:02:24.3869474Z         some part of the dotted name is a package, and the rest is an object
2025-11-20T21:02:24.3869786Z         somewhere within that package, possibly nested inside other objects.
2025-11-20T21:02:24.3870089Z         Because the place where the package stops and the object hierarchy starts
2025-11-20T21:02:24.3870368Z         can't be inferred by inspection, repeated attempts to import must be done
2025-11-20T21:02:24.3870481Z         with this form.
2025-11-20T21:02:24.3870585Z     
2025-11-20T21:02:24.3870853Z         In the second form, the caller makes the division point clear through the
2025-11-20T21:02:24.3871134Z         provision of a single colon: the dotted name to the left of the colon is a
2025-11-20T21:02:24.3871409Z         package to be imported, and the dotted name to the right is the object
2025-11-20T21:02:24.3871706Z         hierarchy within that package. Only one import is needed in this form. If
2025-11-20T21:02:24.3871974Z         it ends with the colon, then a module object is returned.
2025-11-20T21:02:24.3872188Z

2025-11-20T21:02:24.4163253Z         hierarchy within that package. Only one import is needed in this form. If
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4163425Z         it ends with the colon, then a module object is returned.
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4163495Z

2025-11-20T21:02:24.4318484Z         W(.W)*:(W(.W)*)?
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4318541Z     
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4318725Z         The first form is intended for backward compatibility only. It assumes that
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4318873Z         some part of the dotted name is a package, and the rest is an object
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4319032Z         somewhere within that package, possibly nested inside other objects.
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4319205Z         Because the place where the package stops and the object hierarchy starts
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4319371Z         can't be inferred by inspection, repeated attempts to import must be done
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4319446Z         with this form.
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4319508Z     
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4319665Z         In the second form, the caller makes the division point clear through the
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4319837Z         provision of a single colon: the dotted name to the left of the colon is a
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4319993Z         package to be imported, and the dotted name to the right is the object
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4320162Z         hierarchy within that package. Only one import is needed in this form. If
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4320299Z         it ends with the colon, then a module object is returned.
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4320357Z     
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4320531Z         The function will return an object (which might be a module), or raise one
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4320611Z         of the following exceptions:
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4320671Z     
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4320799Z         ValueError - if `name` isn't in a recognised format
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4320990Z         ImportError - if an import failed when it shouldn't have
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4321171Z         AttributeError - if a failure occurred when traversing the object hierarchy
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4321314Z                          within the imported package to get to the desired object.
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4321375Z         """
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4321458Z         global _NAME_PATTERN
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4321536Z         if _NAME_PATTERN is None:
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4321647Z             # Lazy import to speedup Python startup time
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4321720Z             import re
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4321819Z             dotted_words = r'(?!\d)(\w+)(\.(?!\d)(\w+))*'
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4321946Z             _NAME_PATTERN = re.compile(f'^(?P<pkg>{dotted_words})'
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4322059Z                                        f'(?P<cln>:(?P<obj>{dotted_words})?)?$',
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4322145Z                                        re.UNICODE)

2025-11-20T21:02:24.4322513Z             raise ValueError(f'invalid format: {name!r}')
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4322587Z         gd = m.groupdict()
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4322661Z         if gd.get('cln'):
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4322804Z             # there is a colon - a one-step import is all that's needed
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4322905Z             mod = importlib.import_module(gd['pkg'])
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4322985Z             parts = gd.get('obj')

2025-11-20T21:02:24.4323155Z         else:
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4323282Z             # no colon - have to iterate to find the package boundary
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4323372Z             parts = name.split('.')
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4323452Z             modname = parts.pop(0)
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4323554Z             # first part *must* be a module/package.
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4323650Z             mod = importlib.import_module(modname)
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4323720Z             while parts:
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4323803Z                 p = parts[0]
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4323879Z                 s = f'{modname}.{p}'
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4323943Z                 try:

2025-11-20T21:02:24.4324118Z                     parts.pop(0)
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4324191Z                     modname = s
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4324277Z                 except ImportError:
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4324346Z                     break
2025-11-20T21:02:24.4324496Z         # if we reach this point, mod is the module, already imported, and

2025-11-20T21:02:25.2055748Z         it ends with the colon, then a module object is returned.
2025-11-20T21:02:25.2055817Z     
2025-11-20T21:02:25.2055986Z         The function will return an object (which might be a module), or raise one
2025-11-20T21:02:25.2056074Z         of the following exceptions:

2025-11-20T21:02:25.2058144Z         if gd.get('cln'):
